$comment: The threat register (SEC-001): every threat of 10 §3 tied to its control, the epic/story that builds it, and the SEC story whose tests prove it. register.test.ts checks this file on every build with the rules of test/support/register-check.ts (10 §2, §3, §5). Status follows the backlog: "proven" when every acceptance criterion of the proving story that the row names (criteria, 1-based; all of them when absent) is ticked; "partly-proven" when tests exist and one of those criteria is not ticked, with each unticked criterion listed in open; "control-not-built" with the phase it is due when there are no tests yet. A test is named by its file: a name without a slash is under tests/security/test, a path with a slash starts at the repository root; the file must exist and name the proving story. Trust boundaries and actors follow 10 §2. specRows quotes the wording of 10 §3 that a row covers (a table row's threat, or a phrase of the prose in §3.4, §3.7 and §3.8); register.test.ts reads docs/spec/10-security.md and fails when a table row, a §3.7 item or a §3.8 sentence has no register row.

review.note: The end-of-phase review and the second-maintainer sign-off are SEC-003; this register and the SEC suite are its inputs. The sign-off is a human step and is not asserted here.

actors.hostile: no, but attribution is only as strong as the host's authentication

actors.trustedFor: holding the user's token; can do whatever that user can

actors.hostile: assume a user will send hand-crafted protocol messages

actors.trustedFor: nothing; also untrusted as input to an assistant model

actors.hostile: assume a worker can be fully compromised by the input it processes, and treat its outputs as hostile
tamper evidence that must hold against the operator needs chain heads anchored outside (08 §12)
